items.title: CJI Surya Kant announces special bench for hearing Ladakh cases pending in Supreme Court
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday announced that he would set up a special bench of the Supreme Court to hear cases from Ladakh pending before the top court. CJI Kant was speaking at the inaugural function of the Ladakh bench of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court . “I will certainly make an arrangement to set up a special bench on one day to hear all cases from the Ladakh region that are pending before the Supreme Court,” CJI Kant said. CJI Kant, however, said the cases should be argued by lawyers from Leh and Kargil. He added that advocates could appear online before the bench from the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's bench in Leh. “The reason is very obvious. I want that every member of the Kargil and Leh bar must feel integrated with this Supreme Court and Supreme Court bar, and you must feel that you don't represent this area alone. You are in fact representative of the bar association of India, and I can say with again assurance that your competence, your ability, and your articulation is as good as members of the Supreme Court bar. items.title: CJI Surya Kant inaugurates J&K High Court's Ladakh bench in Leh
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday inaugurated Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's newly constituted Ladakh bench in Leh. Supreme Court Justices MM Sundresh , PS Narasimha and Arun Palli , along with judges of the High Court, were also present on the occasion. Attorney General for India R Venkatramani and Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena also attended the event. Ladakh bench inauguration - Group photo Hearing of cases at the Ladakh bench will commence from October 21. A division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar is expected to take up five cases on Wednesday. Justice Parihar will also preside over a single bench and hear cases on Thursday and Friday as well. The High Court has identified a total of 75 cases for listing before the bench situated in Leh. The Union government had approved the establishment of the Ladakh bench for the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh in August this year. Following the decision, the High Court on October 5 selected Leh as the place for holding sittings of the High Court in the Union Territory of Ladakh. items.title: Supreme Court calls internet access a fundamental right for children, rejects blanket ban
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday, October 15, held that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual, including children irrespective of their age. A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the right flows from Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, read with Article 19(1)(a), which protects freedom of speech and expression. “We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution,” the court said in its 136-page order. “Our children, irrespective of their age, enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing. The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both,” it added.
